title: When the Salt Sings
premise: Ines Hartwell, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Vess, has spent his life in the Salt Valley where magic cannot follow—until the crown's witch-hunt forces him to shelter a fugitive girl, Sable, whose gift is a living echo of the god's lost voice. As they flee toward the drowned temple where Vess fell silent thirteen years ago, Ines learns his own oath is the seal that keeps the god mute, and breaking it could reignite the war between gods and men. Hunted by the crown's inquisitor and betrayed by his old company, Ines must choose between duty to his sworn brothers and the found family forming around him. At the thirteenth turn of the moon he speaks the god's name aloud, unsealing Vess—not to wage war, but to testify for humanity—and the god's silence ends with a covenant instead of a conflagration.
about_author: Odile Villalobos is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to map imaginary ones. She writes from a house near tidal flats, where she claims the wind dictates her endings.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet him patrolling the Salt Valley's border stones, where magic dies at the salt line, and learn of his silent god and his mercenary company, the Oathbound. A routine escort turns uneasy when a crown herald posts edicts: all gifted persons to be registered or burned. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The herald explains the moon-count: when the moon completes its thirteenth turn, the hunt becomes law. Ines's captain, Brannoc, orders the company to comply; Ines privately visits the shrine where his oath was sworn and hears nothing, as always. Emotional beat: loneliness inside brotherhood.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A fugitive girl with a voice that makes things grow washes into the valley's fishing village, half-drowned, pursued by riders. She hides among salt-dried nets because her gift cannot function there. Emotional beat: desperate relief in a place that mutes her.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Shouldn't Be Here
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finds Sable hiding in the drying sheds; her gift flickers even in the valley—a thing that should be impossible. He should report her. Instead he lies to the village reeve, his first broken rule in eleven years. Emotional beat: the crack where duty begins to split.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Sable recovers in Ines's cottage; he teaches her valley survival while concealing why he knows so much about hunted gifts. She notices his oath-brand and recognizes its sigil from stories of the god-war. Emotional beat: wary trust kindling.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The inquisitor Corvane arrives with the vanguard of the hunt, questioning villagers. Brannoc covers for Ines once—but warns him the company's loyalty has limits. Sable hides beneath the floorboards, her gift straining against the salt like a caged bird. Emotional beat: claustrophobic fear.

chapters.title: The Oathbound Divide
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The company debates: hand over the girl and keep their contracts, or defy the crown. Old debts and old loves surface. Brannoc, who swore beside Ines at the shrine, chooses the contract—and gives Ines one night's head start as a private mercy. Emotional beat: love curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Crossing the Salt Line
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines and Sable slip over the border stones at night. Outside the valley, Sable's gift blooms violently—flowers through frost, birdsong that bends light—and Ines feels his own sealed power stir for the first time. Emotional beat: terror and wonder entwined.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Traveling through hinterlands, they gather unlikely allies: a defrocked hedge-priest, twin smugglers, an old woman who remembers the god-war. Each recognizes something in Sable's voice. Found family begins to form around a campfire. Emotional beat: warmth hard-won.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The inquisitor interrogates the valley, learns of Ines's lie, and uncovers in crown archives that Ines's oath-line descends from the god-sealers. He realizes the fugitive mercenary isn't just hiding a witch—he may be the key to ending magic forever. Emotional beat: cold ambition sharpening.

chapters.title: The Company Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Brannoc and a loyalist squad catch up at a river ford. The confrontation turns violent; Ines refuses to kill his brothers, taking wounds instead, until Sable's voice shatters the ford itself and drowns the fight. Two Oathbound defect to their side. Emotional beat: grief for the family that wasn't.

chapters.title: What Ines Sealed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Around a healing fire, Ines finally confesses: thirteen years ago, child-sworn to Vess, he spoke the binding words during the god-war's last battle—the seal that silenced the god runs through his blood and voice. Sable's gift is the echo leaking through the cracks. Emotional beat: shame met with acceptance.

chapters.title: The Drowned Temple Road
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They push toward the sunken temple where Vess went silent, racing the moon's twelfth turn. Corvane's riders harry them; the hedge-priest dies buying time at a bridge. The group fractures under loss but binds tighter. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: City of Ash Contracts
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the free city of Marrowgate they seek passage by sea; instead they find Brannoc, now contracted to Corvane, waiting in a smoke-filled tavern. Brannoc offers Ines a choice: surrender Sable and be restored, or be named traitor to every guild. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friend's face.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On the twelfth full moon, Sable's gift surges beyond control—her voice now speaks fragments of Vess's thoughts without her consent. She fears becoming a vessel, not a person. Ines promises she will never be used, not even by a god. Emotional beat: identity versus destiny.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Sound
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Corvane ambushes them at the coastal crossing with a bound storm-witch. The battle wrecks the fleet meant to carry them; the twins are captured. Ines unleashes a sliver of his sealed power to save Sable, cracking his oath-brand and feeling Vess stir beneath it. Emotional beat: power as both salvation and threat.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Pale Camp
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The twins await burning in Corvane's camp. Brannoc walks the lines at night, hearing the prisoners sing Sable's spreading song of the silent god. His certainty erodes; he frees them and sends word to Ines: the thirteenth turn rises over the temple, and Corvane means to be there with fire. Emotional beat: redemption chosen late.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The remnant family reaches the drowned temple as the final moon rises, Corvane's army descending behind them. Inside, the seal within Ines resonates with the temple stones; Vess's presence presses against his mind, offering war if freed by force. Emotional beat: standing at the hinge of history.

chapters.title: Corvane's Fire
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The inquisitor fires the temple grove, intending to burn the god's last anchor and end magic by genocide if necessary. Battle erupts among burning cedars; Brannoc's defection turns the field. Corvane seizes Sable as leverage atop the temple steps. Emotional beat: fanaticism meeting its limit.

chapters.title: The Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. To save Sable, Ines does what no sealer ever dared: he willingly breaks his own oath, speaking Vess's true name—not to command the god, but to ask forgiveness. The seal dissolves; Vess returns not as a weapon but as witness, stilling the fire and stripping Corvane's authority with a single spoken truth. Emotional beat: surrender as the ultimate courage.

chapters.title: Covenant of Salt and Voice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Before gods, armies, and ashes, terms are struck: magic will live openly, registered by choice rather than hunted by decree; Sable declines to be Vess's vessel, and the god accepts her as voice, not vessel. Corvane is taken alive to face the covenant he failed to prevent. Emotional beat: awe settling into peace.

chapters.title: When the Salt Sings
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. A year later, the valley's salt line softens so magic can enter gently, by invitation. Ines, no longer mercenary but warden of the new covenant, watches Sable teach gifted children beside his reformed Oathbound brothers. The god is quiet now by contentment, not silence. Emotional beat: belonging, finally earned.
